explanation: Compared against Written on the Wall II (archived copy of cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html and its definitions file wowIIdefs.js, via the Wayback Machine; the live site does not respond), Conjecture 1 (status T): 'If G is a simple connected graph, then L_s(G) ≥ n + 1 − 2μ(G)', with L_s(G) the maximum number of leaves (degree-one vertices of the tree) over all spanning trees, n the number of vertices and μ(G) the matching number; the accompanying note says Fajtlowicz proved it in 1996 'for connected graphs on at least two vertices'. The Lean statement for a connected G on a finite nontrivial vertex type: (n : ℝ) + 1 − 2·matchingNumber G ≤ Ls G. Ls is the sSup of the number of degree-1 vertices over spanning subgraphs whose coercion is a tree, and matchingNumber is the sSup of edge counts over Subgraph matchings; both sets are nonempty and bounded for connected finite G, so these are the true maxima. The Nontrivial hypothesis is needed (for K_1 the bound would read 0 ≥ 2) and matches the source's 'at least two vertices'. Faithful.
